title: JEE Main Physics: Mechanics
description: Mechanics for JEE Main and Class 11 physics: kinematics, laws of motion, energy, momentum, rotation, gravitation, oscillations.

skills.name: Vectors, units and dimensions
keyPoints: A vector has magnitude and direction; add vectors head-to-tail or by components.
Dot product A·B = AB cosθ (scalar); cross product |A×B| = AB sinθ (vector).
Dimensional analysis checks equations: every term must have the same dimensions.
Impulse and momentum both have dimensions [MLT⁻¹].
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: Units and Measurements; Motion in a Plane (vectors)

items.stem: The dimensional formula of impulse is:
If |A + B| = |A − B|, the angle between A and B is:
items.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 4A·B = 0, so A ⟂ B.

skills.name: Motion in a straight line
keyPoints: Equations of motion for constant a: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as.
Distance in the nth second: sₙ = u + a(n − ½).
Slope of x–t graph is velocity; slope of v–t graph is acceleration; area under v–t is displacement.
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: Motion in a Straight Line

items.stem: A car starts from rest with uniform acceleration 2 m/s². Distance covered in the 3rd second:
The area under a velocity–time graph gives:

skills.name: Projectile and relative motion
keyPoints: Resolve motion into independent horizontal (a = 0) and vertical (a = −g) parts.
Time of flight T = 2u sinθ / g; maximum height H = u² sin²θ / 2g; range R = u² sin2θ / g.
Complementary angles (θ and 90° − θ) give the same range; 45° gives maximum range.
Relative velocity: v_AB = v_A − v_B.
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: Motion in a Plane

items.stem: A projectile is launched at 30° with speed 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Its time of flight is:
For the same launch speed, which pair of angles gives equal horizontal range?
items.explanation: R ∝ sin2θ, and sin2θ = sin(180° − 2θ), so complementary angles give equal range.

skills.name: Newton's laws and free-body diagrams
keyPoints: Net force = rate of change of momentum; for constant mass F = ma.
Draw a free-body diagram for each body; write ΣF = ma along chosen axes.
In a lift accelerating up at a, the normal force is N = m(g + a); down: m(g − a).
Action and reaction act on different bodies.
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: Laws of Motion

skills.name: Friction and constrained motion
keyPoints: Static friction adjusts up to μₛN; kinetic friction = μₖN opposes relative motion.
On an incline, a block is about to slide when tanθ = μₛ (angle of repose).
Check whether the applied force exceeds limiting friction before assuming motion.
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: Laws of Motion (friction)

items.stem: A block on an incline is just about to slide when the incline angle is θ. The coefficient of static friction is:
items.explanation: mg sinθ = μₛ mg cosθ ⇒ μₛ = tanθ.

items.stem: A 5 kg block on a rough floor (μₖ = 0.2, g = 10 m/s²) is pushed with 20 N horizontally while sliding. Its acceleration is:
items.explanation: Friction = 0.2 × 50 = 10 N; net = 10 N; a = 10/5 = 2 m/s².

skills.name: Circular motion
keyPoints: Centripetal acceleration a = v²/r = ω²r, directed towards the centre.
Centripetal force is the net inward force (tension, friction, normal, gravity) - not a new force.
For a string in a vertical circle, minimum speed at the top is √(gR); at the bottom √(5gR).
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: Motion in a Plane (uniform circular motion)

items.stem: A particle moves in a circle of radius 2 m at a constant speed of 4 m/s. Its centripetal acceleration is:
Minimum speed at the top of a vertical circle of radius R for a string to stay taut:
items.explanation: At the top with T = 0: mg = mv²/R ⇒ v = √(gR).

skills.name: Work, energy and power
keyPoints: Work W = F·d = Fd cosθ; work-energy theorem: W_net = ΔKE.
Spring potential energy U = ½kx²; gravitational PE near Earth = mgh.
Mechanical energy is conserved when only conservative forces do work.
Power P = dW/dt = F·v.
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: Work, Energy and Power

skills.name: Momentum, collisions and centre of mass
keyPoints: With no external force, total linear momentum is conserved.
Elastic collisions conserve kinetic energy too; perfectly inelastic: bodies stick together.
Equal masses in a 1-D elastic collision exchange velocities.
Centre of mass: r_cm = Σmᵢrᵢ / Σmᵢ; it moves as if all external forces act on it.
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

items.stem: In a perfectly inelastic collision with no external force, which quantity is always conserved?
items.explanation: Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not in an inelastic collision.

items.stem: A 2 kg ball at 3 m/s collides head-on elastically with an identical ball at rest. Velocities after collision (first, second):
items.explanation: Equal masses in a 1-D elastic collision exchange velocities.

skills.name: Rotational dynamics and rolling
keyPoints: Torque τ = r × F; τ = Iα is the rotational analogue of F = ma.
Moment of inertia: ring MR², disc MR²/2, solid sphere 2MR²/5 (about central axes).
Rolling without slipping: v = ωR; KE = ½mv² + ½Iω².
Angular momentum L = Iω is conserved when net external torque is zero.
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

items.stem: Moment of inertia of a thin ring (mass M, radius R) about its central axis perpendicular to its plane:
items.explanation: All mass is at distance R: I = MR².

skills.name: Gravitation
skills.summary: Newton's law of gravitation, orbits, escape speed
keyPoints: F = GMm/r²; surface gravity g = GM/R².
Orbital speed v₀ = √(GM/r); escape speed vₑ = √(2GM/R).
Gravitational PE U = −GMm/r; total energy of a circular orbit = −GMm/2r.

items.stem: Escape speed from a planet of mass M and radius R is:
If Earth's radius shrank to half with mass unchanged, g at its surface would become:
items.explanation: g = GM/R² ∝ 1/R², so halving R gives 4g.

skills.name: Simple harmonic motion
keyPoints: SHM: a = −ω²x; x = A sin(ωt + φ).
Maximum speed Aω at the mean position; maximum acceleration Aω² at the extremes.
Spring-mass T = 2π√(m/k); simple pendulum T = 2π√(L/g).

skills.name: Properties of solids and fluids
keyPoints: Young's modulus Y = stress/strain.
Pressure in a fluid increases with depth: P = P₀ + ρgh.
Bernoulli's equation expresses conservation of energy along a streamline.
Stokes' law: viscous drag 6πηrv; terminal velocity ∝ r².
resources: NCERT Class 11 Physics: Mechanical Properties of Solids; Mechanical Properties of Fluids

items.stem: Bernoulli's principle is a statement of conservation of:
items.explanation: It is an energy balance per unit volume along a streamline.
